title: Electric Agents
subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log
throughline: One entity, woken into an agent loop, with every step appended to its own durable stream and observable from anywhere.

chapters.title: An Entity Is a Stream
chapters.blurb: Register an entity type, spawn an instance at a slash type slash id address, and watch its whole life become one durable stream.

story.title: An Entity Is a Stream
story.subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log

steps.title: An Entity Is a Stream
steps.narration: Every agent in **Electric Agents** is an *entity* — an addressable, schema-typed unit of state whose session lives on a durable stream.
steps.say: Every agent here is an entity, an addressable unit of state, and its whole life lives on one durable stream.
steps.coverSubtitle: One addressable unit of state, one durable stream of events.

steps.title: The registry of types
steps.narration: You start a registry with `createEntityRegistry()`. It maps type names to definitions — the catalog of every kind of agent your system can run.
steps.say: You start with a registry. Create entity registry gives you a catalog that maps type names to definitions, one entry for every kind of agent.

steps.title: Define a type
steps.narration: `registry.define("assistant", { description, state?, handler })` registers a type. The definition declares its description, its optional state, and the handler that runs when it wakes.
steps.say: You define a type by calling registry define. You name it assistant, give it a description, optional state, and a handler that runs whenever the entity wakes.

steps.title: Spawn an instance
steps.narration: From a type you spawn **instances** at `/{type}/{id}` — an addressable unit of state, for example `/assistant/abc`.
steps.say: From that type you spawn instances. Each one is addressable at slash type slash id, like the assistant abc, a single addressable unit of state.

steps.title: Its own state and handler
steps.narration: Each instance has *its own* state, handler, and event stream — fully isolated from every sibling instance of the same type.
steps.say: Each instance has its own state and its own handler, fully isolated from every other instance of the same type.

steps.title: One stream per entity
steps.narration: An instance's session and state live on a durable **Electric Stream** — a durable, ordered event log. *One stream per entity.*
steps.say: And its session lives on a durable electric stream, a durable ordered event log. One stream per entity.

steps.title: Type, instance, stream
steps.narration: So a type becomes an instance, and that instance's whole life becomes one ordered, durable stream — the foundation everything else builds on.
steps.say: So a type becomes an instance, and that instance turns its whole life into one ordered durable stream. That is the foundation everything else builds on.

chapters.title: Waking an Entity
chapters.blurb: Between wakes an entity is idle; a message, a finished child, a state change, or a timer produces a wake event that invokes its handler.

story.title: Waking an Entity
story.subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log

steps.title: Waking an Entity
steps.narration: Between wakes an entity is idle: no process, no memory. A **wake** is one handler invocation triggered by something outside it.
steps.say: Between wakes an entity is idle. No process, no memory. A wake is one handler invocation, triggered by something happening outside it.
steps.coverSubtitle: Idle until something happens — then a wake invokes the handler.

steps.title: A message arrives
steps.narration: The first source is an **incoming message**. Any external `/send` or another entity's `ctx.send()` appends an `inbox` event.
steps.say: The first thing that can wake an entity is an incoming message. An external send, or another entity calling send, lands in the inbox.

steps.title: A child finishes
steps.narration: A **spawned child** can wake its parent. With `wake: { on: "runFinished" }`, the parent wakes the moment the child's run completes.
steps.say: The second source is a child finishing. When you spawn a child and ask to wake on run finished, the parent wakes the moment that child completes.

steps.title: Observed state changes
steps.narration: An **observed entity** can wake you too. `ctx.observe(entity(url), { wake: { on: "change", collections: [...] } })` re-invokes the handler when a watched collection changes.
steps.say: The third source is a state change. When you observe another entity and ask to wake on change, a change in a watched collection re-invokes your handler.

steps.title: A timer fires
steps.narration: Finally, a **timer or schedule** — a cron entry or a future send — fires at a scheduled time. Schedule entries live on the entity's manifest, so they survive restarts.
steps.say: And the fourth source is a timer. A cron entry or a future send fires at a scheduled time. Because schedules live on the manifest, they survive restarts.

steps.title: The wake is persisted
steps.narration: Whatever the source, a **wake entry is persisted** to the stream before delivery. That's the durability guarantee: a wake that was written will eventually reach a handler.
steps.say: Whatever the source, the wake entry is first written to the stream. That is the durability guarantee. A wake that was written will eventually reach a handler.

steps.title: The handler is invoked
steps.narration: The runtime then invokes `handler(ctx, wake)` with a **WakeEvent**. The handler branches on `wake.type` — `"inbox"`, `"wake"` — and reads `wake.source` and `wake.payload`.
steps.say: The runtime then invokes the handler with a wake event. The handler branches on wake type, inbox or wake, and reads the source and the payload to decide what to do.

chapters.title: The Agent Loop
chapters.blurb: A woken handler calls useAgent and runs the loop; every model call, text delta, and tool invocation is appended to the entity's stream as durable events.

story.title: The Agent Loop
story.subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log

steps.title: The Agent Loop
steps.narration: The core pattern is `ctx.useAgent()` then `ctx.agent.run()`: the LLM runs in a loop until it has nothing left to do, and *all* activity is persisted.
steps.say: The core pattern is use agent, then run. The model runs in a loop until it has nothing left to do, and all of its activity is persisted.
steps.coverSubtitle: Generate, call tools, repeat — and persist every step.

steps.title: Configure the agent
steps.narration: A woken **handler** calls `ctx.useAgent({ systemPrompt, model: "claude-sonnet-4-6", tools })`. This sets up the LLM agent on the entity's behalf.
steps.say: Inside the woken handler you call use agent. You give it a system prompt, a model like claude sonnet, and a list of tools. That configures the agent on the entity's behalf.

steps.title: Run the loop
steps.narration: Then `await ctx.agent.run()` starts **the agent loop**. It blocks until the agent finishes everything it set out to do.
steps.say: Then you await agent run. That starts the agent loop, and it blocks until the agent has finished everything it set out to do.

steps.title: Generate text
steps.narration: The loop calls the **LLM provider** — `claude-sonnet-4-6` — which generates text and decides what to do next.
steps.say: First the loop calls the model. Claude sonnet generates text and decides what to do next.

steps.title: Call tools
steps.narration: When the model asks for a tool, the loop runs it. Tools come from `ctx.electricTools` spread together with your custom tools — `tools: [...ctx.electricTools, myTool]`.
steps.say: When the model asks for a tool, the loop runs it. The tools come from the electric tools the runtime provides, spread together with your own custom tools.

steps.title: Every step appended
steps.narration: Here's the magic: every step — *model call, text delta, tool invocation, error* — is routed through the projection and appended to the entity's **stream** as durable events.
steps.say: And here is the magic. Every step, every model call, text delta, tool invocation, and error, is routed through the projection and appended to the entity's stream as a durable event.

steps.title: Durable and replayable
steps.narration: Because the whole loop is durable events, agents *scale to zero* and survive restarts, and any session can be replayed or forked from any point.
steps.say: Because the whole loop becomes durable events, agents scale to zero and survive restarts. Any session can be replayed, or forked from any point.

chapters.title: The Stream as a Database
chapters.blurb: The stream is projected into a typed local DB; writes go through ctx.db.actions and append events, reads come from ctx.db.collections.

story.title: The Stream as a Database
story.subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log

steps.title: The Stream as a Database
steps.narration: The runtime projects the stream into a typed local DB — an **EntityStreamDB**. Inside a handler that's `ctx.db`.
steps.say: The runtime projects the stream into a typed local database, called an entity stream database. Inside a handler, that database is context dot db.
steps.coverSubtitle: ctx.db — the stream projected into a typed local DB.

steps.title: Writes append events
steps.narration: Writes go through `ctx.db.actions` — and crucially, each write *appends an event to the stream*. The database is just a view; the stream is the truth.
steps.say: Writes go through context dot db dot actions. And the crucial part: every write appends an event to the stream. The database is just a view. The stream is the source of truth.

steps.title: Built-in collections
steps.narration: The stream is projected into **built-in collections** the runtime fills as the agent operates: `runs`, `steps`, `texts`, `toolCalls`, `errors`, `inbox`, and more.
steps.say: The stream is projected into built-in collections that the runtime fills as the agent operates. There are runs, steps, texts, tool calls, errors, the inbox, and many more.

steps.title: Custom state collections
steps.narration: You also add **custom state** collections per entity type — declared with a `schema` and `primaryKey`, written with actions like `ctx.db.actions.items_insert({ row })`.
steps.say: On top of those you add custom state collections, one set per entity type. You declare them with a schema and a primary key, and write to them with actions like items insert.

steps.title: Reads from collections
steps.narration: Reads come from `ctx.db.collections` — `collections.runs.toArray`, `collections.items.get(key)` — querying the projected, typed rows.
steps.say: Reads come from context dot db dot collections. You query the projected typed rows, for example all of the runs, or one item by its key.

steps.title: Typed rows in the handler
steps.narration: Those typed rows flow back to the **handler**, giving live observability into every step of the agent loop — for chat UIs, dashboards, and debugging.
steps.say: Those typed rows flow back into the handler. That gives you live observability into every step of the agent loop, perfect for chat interfaces, dashboards, and debugging.

steps.title: Write down, read across
steps.narration: So `ctx.db.actions` appends to the stream, the stream projects into collections, and `ctx.db.collections` reads them back — one log, two faces.
steps.say: So actions append to the stream, the stream projects into the collections, and the collections read back into your handler. One log, two faces.

chapters.title: Observe From Anywhere
chapters.blurb: An external app loads the same stream into a local DB with the agents client, and re-traces a message through wake, loop, events, and live observers.

story.title: Observe From Anywhere
story.subtitle: The durable runtime for long-lived agents — an agent is a log

steps.title: Observe From Anywhere
steps.narration: Outside the handler, any app can call `createAgentsClient().observe(entity("/type/id"))` to load the stream into a local DB and react in real time.
steps.say: Outside the handler, any app can observe an entity. It loads the same stream into a local database, with the same types, and reacts in real time.
steps.coverSubtitle: The same stream, loaded into any app, reacting in real time.

steps.title: An external client observes
steps.narration: From app code you call `createAgentsClient({ baseUrl })` and `observe(entity("/assistant/abc"))`. It hydrates a local DB with the *same schemas and types* as the handler.
steps.say: From app code you create an agents client and observe an entity. It hydrates a local database using the very same schemas and types the handler uses.

steps.title: A message arrives
steps.narration: Now re-trace the journey. A **message sender** delivers an inbox message to the **entity handler** at `/assistant/abc`.
steps.say: Now let's re-trace the whole journey. A sender delivers a message into the inbox of the entity handler at the assistant abc.

steps.title: The wake runs the loop
steps.narration: That wake invokes the handler, which calls `ctx.useAgent()` and `ctx.agent.run()` — starting the **agent loop**.
steps.say: That wake invokes the handler. It calls use agent and run, which starts the agent loop.

steps.title: Every step becomes events
steps.narration: Every step of that loop is appended to the entity's **stream** as durable events — the same stream from chapter one.
steps.say: Every step of that loop is appended to the entity's stream as durable events. It is the very same stream we started with in chapter one.

steps.title: Observers react live
steps.narration: Because the observed **local DB** mirrors that stream, every new event flows straight to the external **app** in real time — no polling.
steps.say: Because the observed local database mirrors that stream, every new event flows straight to the external app in real time, with no polling.

steps.title: Message, wake, loop, observe
steps.narration: One message becomes a wake, the wake runs the loop, the loop appends events, and every observer sees them live — *an agent is a log.*
steps.say: So one message becomes a wake, the wake runs the loop, the loop appends events, and every observer sees them the instant they happen. An agent is a log.
